chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am with these people, and I depart from them at Maghrib, passing by the mosques. If I descend to pray with them, I will not be able to perform the Adhan, the Iqamah, and the opening of the prayer.' He said: 'Go to your house, remove your outer garments, and if you wish to perform Wudu, perform Wudu and pray, for you are within the time until a quarter of the night.'

key_terms.افْتِتَاحِ الصَّلَاةِ: Opening of the prayer (referring to the initial Takbir or ritual actions)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: Iqamah (second call to prayer, preceding the prayer)
key_terms.رُبُعِ اللَّيْلِ: A quarter of the night (time marker for the end of Maghrib time)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying Maghrib individually if delayed by congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of individual prayer (*Salat al-Fardi*) when delayed by congregational duties, emphasizing that the Maghrib time extends until a quarter of the night (*rub' al-layl*). The Imam’s instruction to remove outer garments highlights the transition from public engagement to private devotion, reinforcing the principle that validity is maintained even if the prayer is performed later than the preferred time (*waqt al-fadila*).
